args.body:
CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL

MEMORANDUM

TO: Board of Directors
FROM: Emerging Companies & Venture Capital Practice Group
DATE: [Current Date]
RE: Analysis of Investor Markup — Convertible Note Purchase Agreement
    Reconciliation Against Board-Approved Term Sheet

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have completed a full reconciliation of the investor's markup of the convertible note purchase agreement (the "Agreement") against the board-approved term sheet and the operative base materials. The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that require attention: (i) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap accompanied by conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket; (ii) an expansion of the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition through carve-outs for regulatory action of precisely the kind flagged in the disclosure schedules; and (iii) a shortened survival period for the core representations. Consistent with the controlling partner instruction, we have evaluated each deviation against the client's negotiation posture: the client is prepared to concede the basket conversion but will treat any reduction to the survival period as a walk-away issue. This memorandum sets forth our detailed analysis, recommends positions, and flags open items for decision.

I. INDEMNIFICATION PROVISIONS — SILENT CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION

A. Deviation Identified

The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap set forth in the board-approved term sheet. The base term sheet caps the investor's indemnification exposure at a defined aggregate amount. The markup lowers that cap without accompanying negotiation commentary. In addition, the markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible structure to a tipping (threshold) basket.

B. Reconciliation Against Base Materials

Pursuant to Schedule 5.2, the company has disclosed a list of retained liabilities. The reduction of the indemnification cap operates in concert with the basket conversion to materially narrow counterparty exposure. Under a deductible basket, the indemnitor bears all losses once the aggregate loss exceeds the threshold; under a tipping basket, once the threshold is crossed, the indemnitor's exposure begins from the first dollar. The conversion from deductible to tipping is, in isolation, a less objectionable change because it provides for full recovery once threshold is met. However, the simultaneous reduction of the cap means the total recoverable amount is significantly constrained.

C. Recommendation

Consistent with the controlling partner instruction that the client will concede the basket conversion, we recommend accepting the conversion from deductible to tipping basket. However, we strongly recommend **rejecting** the silent reduction of the indemnification cap. The cap had been expressly approved by the board in the term sheet. Any reduction represents an unapproved economic concession. We recommend countering with the original cap amount, or in the alternative, accepting a modest reduction only if the client is willing to prioritize expediency over preserving the economic terms. The retained liabilities disclosed in Schedule 5.2 make cap preservation particularly important, as several such liabilities fall squarely within the scope of the indemnification obligations.

II. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS

A. Deviation Identified

The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Specifically, the markup carves out from the MAE definition any impacts arising from regulatory investigations, enforcement proceedings, or other governmental action.

B. Intersection with Disclosure Schedules

As disclosed in Schedule 3.7, the company has two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries fall squarely within the scope of the carve-out proposed by the counterparty. By excluding regulatory-driven adverse effects from what constitutes an MAE, the markup would effectively insulate the investor from the very risk that Schedule 3.7 already flags. This creates a tension: the disclosure schedule faithfully surfaces the regulatory inquiries as a risk factor, but the markup would remove the contractual consequence of that risk materializing.

C. Analysis

The carve-out is materially adverse to the company. Under the board-approved term sheet, the MAE definition is drafted broadly enough to capture material regulatory impacts, consistent with firm precedent for venture-stage financing transactions. The proposed carve-out would permit the investor to decline to close (if MAE serves as a closing condition) or to assert that regulatory developments do not constitute an MAE relieving the investor of obligations, even where such developments materially impair the company's value. The fact that two regulatory inquiries are already pending amplifies the risk: the carve-out appears designed to neutralize precisely the disclosure that the company has already made.

D. Recommendation

We recommend **rejecting** the regulatory carve-out to the MAE definition. If the investor insists on narrowing the MAE definition, we propose a counter that: (i) limits any regulatory carve-out to actions initiated after the closing date; (ii) excludes from the carve-out regulatory actions arising from the company's prior or ongoing conduct as disclosed in Schedule 3.7; and/or (iii) requires that any regulatory impact exceeding a materiality threshold still constitute an MAE. Given the disclosure schedule expressly anticipates regulatory exposure, we view removal or significant narrowing of this carve-out as a non-negotiable priority.

III. SURVIVAL PERIOD — SHORTENED LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

A. Deviation Identified

The counterparty's markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations beyond the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B to the base materials.

B. Conflict with Exhibit B

Exhibit B to the base materials establishes the survival matrix for representations and warranties. The markup's shortened limitation period directly contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B. Pursuant to the schedules and exhibits, the survival matrix in Exhibit B is controlling over any general statements contained in the operative materials. The scheduled exceptions therefore strengthen our position that the survival periods cannot be shortened absent a negotiated amendment to Exhibit B itself.

C. Analysis — Walk-Away Issue

Per the controlling partner instruction in the most recent deal correspondence, **any reduction to the survival period is a walk-away issue** for the client. The partner's instruction supersedes any earlier communications expressing a contrary priority. This is therefore a defined deal-breaker. We must communicate clearly to the investor that the survival periods in Exhibit B are non-negotiable and that any reduction will prevent the transaction from closing. The core representations for which the survival period is most critical include the fundamental representations (organization, capitalization, authority) and the regulatory representations intersecting with Schedule 3.7.

D. Recommendation

We recommend **rejecting, without counter**, any reduction to the survival period for core representations. This position is a walk-away threshold. We further recommend that if the investor does not remove this deviation from the markup, we notify the client immediately and prepare for potential termination of negotiations. We should also proceed on the assumption that survival periods for non-core representations may be negotiable, subject to partner guidance, but that reductions to core representation survival are not.

IV. OPEN ITEMS AND DECISION REQUESTS

1. Indemnification Cap: Confirm the maximum cap reduction, if any, the client is willing to accept. Our recommendation is to preserve the board-approved cap in full.

2. MAE Regulatory Carve-Out: Confirm the client's appetite for our proposed narrowing counter-language regarding timing of regulatory actions and the materiality threshold.

3. Survival Period: Confirm that the walk-away position on survival reduction for core representations reflects final client instructions, so that we may communicate this position to the counterparty without reservation.

V. PRIORITIZED DEVIATION SUMMARY

┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────────────────────┐
│ Deviation                │ Recommended Action   │ Priority              │ Risk if Accepted      │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ Indemnification cap      │ Reject cap reduction;│ High                  │ Reduced counterparty  │
│ reduction + basket       │ concede the basket   │                       │ exposure on retained  │
│ conversion (deductible → │ conversion only      │                       │ liabilities per       │
│ tipping)                 │                       │                       │ Schedule 5.2          │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ MAE regulatory carve-out │ Reject; propose      │ High                  │ Investor excused from │
│                          │ narrowing counter    │                       │ obligations upon      │
│                          │                       │                       │ regulatory MAE despite│
│                          │                       │                       │ Schedule 3.7          │
│                          │                       │                       │ disclosures           │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ Survival period          │ Reject outright —    │ Critical /            │ Fundamental risk that │
│ reduction               │ walk-away issue      │ Walk-Away             │ claims under core     │
│                          │ per controlling      │                       │ representations expire│
│                          │ partner instruction  │                       │ prematurely            │
└──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┘

VI. CONCLUSION

The investor's markup contains three material deviations from the board-approved term sheet. Our recommended position is: (1) reject the indemnification cap reduction while conceding the basket conversion, per the controlling partner instruction; (2) reject the MAE regulatory carve-out and counter with narrowing language that protects the company given the disclosed regulatory inquiries; and (3) reject any survival period reduction outright as a walk-away issue. We recommend proceeding with the position set forth above and communicating the walk-away thresholds to the counterparty in the next round of negotiations.

Please advise on the open items and decision requests set forth in Section IV.

Respectfully submitted,
Emerging Companies & Venture Capital Practice Group
